title: The Heiress Convicted of Her Parents' Murder
hook: In 2002, a 19-year-old kissed her parents goodnight — then unlocked the door for the men who would beat them to death — a crime she was later convicted of.

visual_context.setting: upper-class home in Sao Paulo Brazil

lines.text: In 2002, a 19-year-old kissed her parents goodnight — then unlocked the door for the men who would beat them to death — a crime she was later convicted of.
Her name was Suzane von Richthofen. On the surface: wealthy, intelligent, the perfect daughter of a respected engineer in Sao Paulo.
But her parents disapproved of her boyfriend, Daniel — and prosecutors said the inheritance became the motive.
On Halloween night, she let Daniel and his brother into the house. While Manfred and Marisia slept, the brothers struck them with iron bars.
Then they staged a robbery — drawers pulled open, valuables scattered — and Suzane took her younger brother out for ice cream in what investigators described as an attempt to build an alibi.
It almost worked. But police noticed the burglars ignored the cash in plain sight, and the family dog never barked.
Within days, police said she had confessed. The trial gripped Brazil — a case that left the country asking how someone so privileged could do this.
Suzane was sentenced to 39 years. She has since been released to open prison — a free woman who, commentators and parts of the Brazilian press have said, never showed real remorse.
